title: Fakes
description: The fake handlers' files (SPEC §5.4, §6.2), after YAML parsing. A key is the question or command text after interpolation, exactly as it would be sent: a question has run outputs named in backticks (SPEC §3.5). Or it's `line:N` for the statement on line N of SKILL.md, or `Section.var` for the statement in that section that binds var, or `Section.ask` for the section's only ask (SPEC §5.4). A stable key wins over `line:N`, which wins over the text. Each fake scenario directory also holds `expected-exit`: the exit code the run must end with (PLAN.md §3).

answers.description: answers.yaml. A probs object keyed by option id, with optional `unassigned`, is passed to the core as the backend's answer, valid or not. `unsure` is a uniform answer over the options, which is always a tie, so the gate fails. `unavailable` is a backend failure (ask_unavailable).

commands.description: commands.yaml: how each command ends. A list is used in order, one result per run of the command, with the last repeating: a loop that re-reads usage can see it fall. An unmatched command is E-FAKE-UNMATCHED; no real command ever runs.

result.description: A plain string or number is shorthand for {exit: 0, stdout: <its text>}.

ms.description: Simulated duration. Under --fake-exec the host's clock advances by it, so deadline scenarios can be written.
